text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Britain's envoy on the Cyprus problem Sir David Hannay believes direct talks between the two sides will be called this summer. "This time we won't trip over," he told BBC radio.

- Right-wing Disy vice-chairman Nicos Anastassiades disagrees with statements made by incumbent leader Yiannakis Matsis, who has criticised the government for keeping politicians in the dark over developments on the Cyprus issue.
- The Democratic Party in Larnaca is on the verge of a split. Members criticise the party's leadership for remaining in the government.
- Suspicious movements of motorcyclists have been noted close to the ceasefire line in the Aglandjia suburb of Nicosia.
- Greece and Cyprus are willing to show goodwill to Turkey in an attempt to force Ankara to reveal its true intentions as far as the Cyprus issue and the Greco-Turkish differences are concerned.
- Greece will not become a protectorate of Turkey, warns Greece's Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos in a newspaper interview.
